MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Children's Hospital
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date] 2013
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRING PHYSICIAN
Dr. [redacted name]
Department of Pediatric Neurology

CLINICAL INDICATION
Diagnostic testing for SMARD1 (Spinal muscular atrophy with respiratory distress)

TEST PERFORMED
Direct DNA Sequencing of IGHMBP2 Gene

METHODOLOGY
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes using standard protocols. Direct DNA sequencing of the IGHMBP2 gene was performed, covering all 15 exons (exons 1-15) including flanking intronic sequences and splice sites. Sequencing was performed using fluorescent dye-terminator Sanger sequencing on an Applied Biosystems 3730xl DNA Analyzer. Sequence data was analyzed using GeneAnalyzer software and compared to the reference sequence NM_002180.2.

TECHNICAL NOTES
- Detection rate: Approximately 95% for pathogenic variants in this locus
- This assay detects point mutations and small insertions/deletions
- Large deletions/duplications would not be detected by this methodology
- Variants in deep intronic or regulatory regions are not assessed

RESULTS

IGHMBP2 Gene Analysis (chromosome 11q13-q21):

No clearly pathogenic mutations were detected.

Three heterozygous variants of uncertain significance were identified:

1. c.741C>T (p.Ala247Ala)
   - Synonymous variant
   - Heterozygous
   - Classification: Variant of Uncertain Significance

2. c.1104C>T (p.Tyr368Tyr)
   - Synonymous variant
   - Heterozygous
   - Classification: Variant of Uncertain Significance

3. c.1418+18A>G
   - Intronic variant
   - Heterozygous
   - Classification: Variant of Uncertain Significance

INTERPRETATION
No clearly pathogenic mutations were identified in the IGHMBP2 gene. The three heterozygous variants detected (c.741C>T, c.1104C>T, and c.1418+18A>G) were assessed using GeneAnalyzer software and classified as variants of uncertain significance. These variants are assessed as unlikely to be pathogenic based on current evidence.

This result significantly reduces the likelihood of SMARD1 diagnosis due to IGHMBP2 mutations to less than 1%. However, it should be noted that approximately 5% of pathogenic variants may not be detected by this methodology.

CLINICAL CORRELATION
SMARD1 (Spinal Muscular Atrophy with Respiratory Distress type 1) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the IGHMBP2 gene. The absence of clearly pathogenic variants in this analysis makes the diagnosis of SMARD1 due to IGHMBP2 mutations unlikely in this patient.

RECOMMENDATIONS
- Consider that other unidentified genetic loci may cause a SMARD phenotype
- Clinical correlation is recommended
- If clinical suspicion remains high, consider:
  • Deletion/duplication analysis of IGHMBP2
  • Broader genetic testing approaches (e.g., neuromuscular gene panel or exome sequencing)
  • Re-evaluation of the clinical diagnosis

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The laboratory is certified under CLIA to perform high-complexity testing.

Report Authorized By:
[redacted name], Ph.D., FACMG
Laboratory Director
Board Certified Clinical Molecular Geneticist
